snippet.title: Sourav Joshi drew sketches for $5. Now he has 42 million subscribers
snippet.description:
An artist designs his own path for success 🎨

In 2017, @souravjvlogs began uploading his art process to YouTube, showing viewers how to realistically draw everything from legendary Bollywood stars to iconic movie characters. In 2020, he took on a challenge to create 365 vlogs in 365 days, giving a unique and personal look into his family life (including their new puppy Oreo) – and was catapulted into the limelight.

Now, Sourav has 42 million subscribers and has achieved a whopping 24 BILLION lifetime views. The secret to his success? He says there is NO secret – just showing his honest family life as it is is what his fans have so strongly connected to. Go behind the scenes of his transformation from artist to daily vlogger to back to being art himself.

snippet.title: Golf Is About To Change Forever
snippet.description:
Golf is in the middle of a rewrite, and a five-and-a-half-hour second round at the 2026 PGA Championship shows its biggest problem still hasn't been solved.

Scottie Scheffler says his group didn't gain a single second on the clock. Tiger Woods says a ball rollback should have happened a long time ago, and Jack Nicklaus took his worries about the ball to the rule-makers in 1977. Justin Thomas asks what time par even is.

So what should golf actually change?

This video looks at how the rules of golf have changed, from one rulebook in 1952 to the 2019 rewrite and the two-hole U.S. Open playoff, and how basketball, baseball and tennis redesigned themselves around the people watching.

Then we debate six ideas on the table: a shot clock, publishing every player's stroke time, rangefinders, strokes instead of fines, rolling back the ball, and 54 holes instead of 72.

Greg Norman, Nick Faldo, Jean van de Velde and Rory McIlroy all come up along the way.

On August 21, 1986, something horrifying happened at Lake Nyos in Cameroon. In a single night, approximately 1,746 people lost their lives. There was no massive explosion, no fire, and no visible destruction. Just a mysterious cloud that silently spread through nearby villages, leaving thousands of people and animals dead.

But here's the truly disturbing part…

Beneath the peaceful surface of this lake, enormous amounts of Carbon Dioxide had been silently accumulating for years. And when this invisible gas was suddenly released, it triggered one of the strangest natural disasters in history — a phenomenon known as a Limnic Eruption.

But how can an ordinary-looking lake store enough invisible gas to wipe out entire villages?

Discover the chilling story of the 1986 Lake Nyos disaster and the scientific mystery hidden beneath its waters.

snippet.title: Usunąłem Koreę Północną z historii. Samsung wrócił do ryb
snippet.description:
Co by było, gdyby Korea Północna zniknęła z historii? Bierzemy gumkę i ścieramy kreskę, którą dwóch amerykańskich pułkowników narysowało w pół godziny na mapie z National Geographic. Tylko że bez tej kreski czołgi jadą aż do morza, a bez Północnej nie ma Południowej. Ani Samsunga.

A w prawdziwej historii kreska została i przyniosła wojnę. Ponad tysiąc koreańskich sierot trafiło wtedy do Płakowic na Dolnym Śląsku.

Pół żartem, pół serio: śmiejemy się z propagandy i z historii, nie z ludzi, którzy tam żyją. Scenariusz „co by było” jest zmyślony, fakty w nim są prawdziwe.

Gumka jest u ciebie: ścierasz czy zostawiasz? Pisz w komentarzu.

snippet.title: 6 NIÑOS, 15 meses solos en una ISLA desierta 🌊
snippet.description:
6 niños pasaron 15 meses solos en una isla desierta… y pasó justo lo contrario que en «El señor de las moscas». 🌊

En junio de 1965, seis alumnos de un internado de Tonga se escaparon en un barco robado. Una tormenta los dejó 8 días a la deriva hasta 'Ata, una isla volcánica vacía desde 1863. Allí se organizaron por turnos, mantuvieron el fuego encendido más de un año y se cuidaron entre ellos hasta que, en septiembre de 1966, los rescató el pescador australiano Peter Warner. Y al volver a casa… acabaron en la cárcel.

▶️ Mira también: ¿Por qué el país CHILE tiene forma de chile? 🌶 https://www.youtube.com/shorts/72qIrwV8RRo

Fuentes: Wikipedia (en) «Tongan castaways», «ʻAta» y «Peter Warner» · Rutger Bregman, «The real Lord of the Flies» (The Guardian, 9-5-2020) · Boating NZ, «Surviving Ata» · The Spinoff (17-5-2020). Las edades varían según la fuente (13-16 según Bregman; 16-18 según Lavin, 1966).
